source.title: Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey with Empirical Insights from the Qwen 1.5 1.8B Model

record.file_problem: none; full post text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own Qwen 1.5 1.8B unlearning experiments and evaluates unlearning-related loss and general-task performance, using measures different from a direct test of recovered knowledge.
record.gate_note: The adversarial-attack figures and results attributed to RWKU and Breaking Chains are sourced from other work, so they are not this study's results. The post describes neuron-level analysis but reports no neuron-level result. Its Mink++ values are reported as evidence of residual traces, but are not a direct behavioral test of prompt-based recovery.
record.test_reason: The post reports its own GA and DPO unlearning runs on Qwen 1.5 1.8B, with general-ability scores (TriviaQA, BBH) after unlearning. These bear only on Version A's general-ability clause. Targeted-knowledge accuracy and attack recovery are not measured. The attack figures are copied from RWKU and Breaking Chains, not the authors' own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that GA and DPO can erase targeted data but damage general performance (GA catastrophically), and that residual traces remain. Their further claim that deeper prompts can coax out knowledge is asserted from mink++ values, not tested by their own experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The post reports GA and DPO experiments on Qwen 1.5 1.8B but does not give enough training details to establish that either follows a specific original recipe. It describes a PyTorch training loop and links a GitHub repository.

fits_no_version.finding: Mink_0.1 and Mink++ membership-style scores on Forget vs Retain Mia, from an unspecified unlearning method, interpreted by the authors as residual knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership-inference scores after unlearning differ only slightly between forget and retain sets, which the authors read as residual traces.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient ascent changes the loss on Forget Mia (–2.807) and Retain Mia (–2.547).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient ascent shifts loss on both forget and retain data, with no targeted-accuracy measure.

record.problems: The post does not provide uncertainty estimates or enough methodological detail to reproduce the experiments from the text alone. It reports no direct targeted-knowledge accuracy or own adversarial-prompt recovery test. The attack figures are attributed to other studies, and the unlearning method associated with the Minkowski results is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible results left out. Attack results in Figure 2 and the GA+RT results in Figure 3 are attributed to other work and were excluded.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy relative to chance, and whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
All; neuron analysis is mentioned but no result is reported.
All; residual-knowledge claims rest on mink++ values, not on prompting tests.

record.verdict_notes: A student survey post with one small, internally inconsistent results table: GA and DPO report the identical 0.037 BBH score, and the Forget/Retain column labels are applied to TriviaQA and BBH. No uncertainty is reported. Treat its evidence as weak.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy relative to chance or test whether simple attacks recover knowledge. Its own results bear on unlearning loss and preservation of general-task performance.
No small-set fine-tuning or relearning recovery experiment is reported.
No activation-direction ablation or reported internal-edit experiment is provided.
No own behavioral test of recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information is reported.
No robust counter-method is tested against the listed attacks.

relationships.condition: GA and DPO unlearning on Qwen 1.5 1.8B (RWKU-style forget set)
relationships.reason: TriviaQA EM falls to 0.0 and BBH EM to 0.037 (vs 0.45), so these methods did not keep general ability (r3, r4, r5). These are not the original sources' methods, and the numbers are ambiguous and possibly duplicated, so this qualifies A rather than challenging it.
relationships.display_finding: Reported TriviaQA exact match fell to 0.0 and BBH exact match to 0.037 from 0.45, although the figures were ambiguous and possibly duplicated.
